canonical_answers: Solving m dv/dt=-bv gives v(t)=v₀e^{-bt/m} and x(t)=mv₀(1-e^{-bt/m})/b.

payload.text: A mass m moves through a medium with drag force F=-bv and initial speed v₀.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict how the observable changes when the defining scale parameter is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

criteria.description: Doubling b halves the time constant τ=m/b, so v(t)=v₀e^{-2bt/m} decays twice as fast, and the total stopping distance x(∞)=mv₀/b is halved since x(∞)∝1/b.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how the inverse dependence of the time constant τ=m/b on b, given that m and v₀ are unchanged, justifies why doubling b halves both τ and the stopping distance.

criteria.description: Explain how the inverse dependence of the time constant τ=m/b on b, given that m and v₀ are unchanged, justifies why doubling b halves both τ and the stopping distance.
required_evidence: τ=m/b is inversely proportional to b
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
